results.title: Outer automorphism group of a free group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators. Its outer automorphism group $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ is the quotient of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ by the normal subgroup generated by the inner automorphisms. Since the inner automorphisms already form a normal subgroup $\mathrm{Inn}(F_n)$, this is $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n) / \mathrm{Inn}(F_n)$.

results.title: Large Zsigmondy prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ and $p$ be natural numbers. Then $p$ is a large Zsigmondy prime for $(a, b, n)$ when $p$ is a primitive prime divisor of the term $a^n - b^n$ of the integer sequence $(a^m - b^m)_{m \ge 0}$, that is, $n \ge 1$, $p$ is prime, $p$ divides $a^n - b^n$ and $p$ divides no $a^m - b^m$ with $1 \le m < n$, and moreover $p^2$ divides $a^n - b^n$ or $p > n + 1$.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Flat Littlewood polynomials exist

results.title: Fuel-bounded Ulam test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $f$ (the fuel) and a word $w$ in the letters $0$ and $1$, the test returns false when $f = 0$. With fuel $f + 1$ it returns true when $w$ has length $1$; otherwise it returns true exactly when there is exactly one $k$ with $1 \le k < |w|$ such that the prefix $w_1 \cdots w_k$ and the suffix $w_{k+1} \cdots w_{|w|}$ are distinct and both pass the test with fuel $f$.

results.title: Ulam words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Ulam words are finite words over the alphabet $\{0, 1\}$, defined by recursion on the length. The empty word is not an Ulam word, and the two words $0$ and $1$ of length $1$ are Ulam words. A word $w$ of length at least $2$ is an Ulam word if and only if there is exactly one way to write $w = uv$ with $u$ and $v$ nonempty, distinct Ulam words.

results.title: Ulam words of length at most three
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty word is not an Ulam word, and both words $0$ and $1$ of length one are Ulam words. The Ulam words of length two are exactly $01$ and $10$, and the Ulam words of length three are exactly $001$, $011$, $100$ and $110$.

results.title: Ulam words of length four: examples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The words $0001$ and $1011$ are Ulam words, while $0011$ and $0110$ are not.

results.title: Number of Ulam words of a given length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\#U_n$ denotes the number of Ulam words of length $n$, that is, of words $w_1 \cdots w_n$ of length $n$ in the letters $0$ and $1$ that are Ulam words.

results.title: Numbers of short Ulam words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are $2$, $2$, $4$ and $8$ Ulam words of length $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ respectively: $\#U_1 = 2$, $\#U_2 = 2$, $\#U_3 = 4$ and $\#U_4 = 8$, where $\#U_n$ is the number of Ulam words of length $n$.

results.title: Ulam words in a residue class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $N$ and $n$ and a residue class $a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, this is the number of Ulam words $w$ of length $n$ in the letters $0$ and $1$ whose binary value $\pi(w)$, read with the most significant letter first, lies in the class $a$ modulo $N$. For $N = 0$, $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z}$ is $\mathbb{Z}$ and the condition is $\pi(w) = a$.

results.title: Residues of the Ulam words of length 2 modulo 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Read the Ulam words of length $2$ as binary numerals, most significant letter first. None of their values is congruent to $0$ modulo $3$, exactly one is congruent to $1$, and exactly one is congruent to $2$.

results.title: Sorted binary values of Ulam words

results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the list $u_1 < u_2 < \dots < u_k$ of the distinct binary values $\pi(w)$, read with the most significant letter first, of the Ulam words $w$ of length $n$, in increasing order.

results.title: Binary values of the Ulam words of length 3

results.title: Stages of the discrete Sierpiński triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stages $S_n \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ of the discrete Sierpiński triangle are defined by $S_0 = \{(2, 1)\}$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n \cup (S_n + (2^n, 0)) \cup (S_n + (2^n, 2^n))$, where $S + (u, v) = \{(x + u, y + v) : (x, y) \in S\}$ denotes a translate.

results.title: The discrete Sierpiński triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The discrete Sierpiński triangle is the set $\mathcal{S} = \bigcup_{n \ge 0} S_n \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, the union of all the stages $S_n$ of the discrete Sierpiński triangle.

results.title: The first stage of the discrete Sierpiński triangle
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Ulam words with a block of four ones
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a + b \ge 1$, the binary word $0^a 1111 0^b$ ($a$ zeros, then four ones, then $b$ zeros) is an Ulam word if and only if $a + b \equiv 1 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Square of the Ulam word count is at most a block sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, $(\#U_n)^2 \le \sum_{i=n}^{2n} \#U_i$, where $\#U_i$ is the number of Ulam words of length $i$.

results.title: Ulam words with three leading ones
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 3$, the word $1^3 0^{n-3}$ (three ones followed by $n - 3$ zeros) is an Ulam word if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ or $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Linear lower bound on the number of Ulam words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 6$, the number of Ulam words of length $n$ is at least $2n + 4$.

results.title: Exponential lower bound for Ulam word counts along a subsequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\#U_n$ be the number of Ulam words of length $n$ and $\alpha_0 = (\#U_{30} / (2 \cdot 31))^{1/30}$. For every real $\alpha$ with $1 < \alpha < \alpha_0$, every real $C$ and every natural number $N$, there is some $n \ge N$ with $C \alpha^n \le \#U_n$; that is, $\limsup_{n \to \infty} \#U_n / \alpha^n = \infty$.

results.title: The inverse Ulam density has the order of the mean gap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $U_n$ be the set of Ulam words of length $n$, and let $\mu_g(n)$ be the mean gap of the binary values of the words in $U_n$. Then $2^n / |U_n|$ (the reciprocal of the density $|U_n| / 2^n$) and $\mu_g(n)$ have the same order of growth as $n \to \infty$: there are constants $c, C > 0$ such that $c \, \mu_g(n) \le 2^n / |U_n| \le C \, \mu_g(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

results.title: Counting Ulam words with a single one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the number of $a \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ for which the word $0^a 1 0^{n-1-a}$ ($a$ zeros, then a one, then $n - 1 - a$ zeros) is an Ulam word equals $2^{s_2(n-1)}$, where $s_2(m)$ is the sum of the binary digits of $m$. This number is the term $G(n - 1)$ of Gould's sequence.

results.title: Ulam words with a block of two ones
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the binary word $0^a 11 0^b$ ($a$ zeros, then two ones, then $b$ zeros) is an Ulam word if and only if $a + b$ is odd.

results.title: Ulam words with one 101 block

results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a + b \ge 2$, the binary word $0^a 101 0^b$ ($a$ zeros, then the letters $1, 0, 1$, then $b$ zeros) is an Ulam word if and only if $a + b$ is odd.

results.title: Parity criterion for Ulam words with a single one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the binary word $0^a 1 0^b$ ($a$ zeros, then a one, then $b$ zeros) is an Ulam word if and only if the binomial coefficient $\binom{a + b}{a}$ is odd.

results.title: Ulam words made of ones followed by zeros
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Uniqueness of the lexicographically largest vertex

results.summary: In a simple walk the lexicographically largest vertex is attained at a unique index.

results.title: Existence of a north-then-west corner
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A closed walk without right turns has a north-then-west corner.

results.title: Two north-then-west corners force a self-intersection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Any two distinct north-then-west corners of `d` force `pos d` to be non-injective.

results.title: Four left turns, given that two corners force a self-intersection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A simple closed walk without right turns has four left turns, assuming that two distinct north-then-west corners force a self-intersection.

results.title: Unit cell to the left of a lattice step

results.title: Steps around a left turn share their left cell
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a left turn, the steps before and after the turn have the same left cell.

results.title: No vertical step through a non-vertex point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vertical step through the point `(c, h)` has `(c, h)` as a vertex; if `(c, h)` is not a walk vertex, no vertical step straddles height `h` on the line `x = c`.

results.title: No horizontal step starts at a non-vertex point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `(c, h)` is not a walk vertex, no horizontal step starts at `x = c` on height `h`.

results.title: Index of a vertical step above a walk vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a simple walk, a vertical step on the segment above the vertex `pos d m` is step `m` or step `m - 1`.

results.title: Index of a horizontal step right of a walk vertex

results.title: Index of a vertical step below a walk vertex
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Index of a horizontal step left of a walk vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a simple walk, a horizontal step on the segment to the left of the vertex `pos d m` is step `m` or step `m - 1`.

results.title: Left cells keep their ray parity on a straight step
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Ray parity of the cell left of a step

results.title: Consecutive steps have the same left parity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple closed walk without right turns, consecutive steps have the same left parity.

results.title: Left parity is constant along a walk without right turns
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple closed walk without right turns, the left parity is the same for every step.

results.title: Vertical steps separating two horizontal neighbour cells

results.title: Parity of upward crossings across a vertical segment

results.title: Ray parity across a vertical segment counts separating steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ray parities of cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` add up to the number of separating vertical steps mod `2`.

results.title: An odd number of vertical steps flips the ray parity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An odd number of vertical steps between cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` flips the ray parity.

results.title: Horizontal steps on a unit segment

results.title: Upward crossings of vertically adjacent cells differ by separating steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The upward crossings from cell `(a, b)` are those from `(a, b + 1)` plus the horizontal steps between the two cells.

results.title: An odd number of horizontal steps flips the ray parity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An odd number of horizontal steps between cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` flips the ray parity.

results.title: $k + 2 \ne k$ in $\mathrm{Fin}\, n$ for $n \ge 3$

results.title: Some north-then-west corner has its below-left cell inside

results.title: Single west run covering the top row

results.title: A single top run makes the top row contiguous

results.title: Top row is contiguous when every top corner starts a single run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If every highest north-then-west corner starts a single top run, the top row is contiguous.

results.title: A north step into a highest vertex is followed by a west step

results.summary: In a closed walk without right turns, a north step arriving at a highest vertex is followed by a west step.

results.title: A west step on the top row is followed by west or south

results.title: A closed walk is not all west steps

results.summary: A closed walk does not consist of west steps only.

results.title: A west run from a highest vertex ends in a south step

results.summary: From a highest vertex where the walk turns west, it makes `J ≥ 1` west steps and then a south step.

results.title: A west run covering the top row is a single top run

results.title: A step changes the x-coordinate by at most one

results.title: Number of crossings of a vertical line

results.title: A closed walk crosses a vertical line equally often left and right
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A walk crosses the line `x = m + 1/2` to the right as often as to the left.

results.title: A closed walk crosses each vertical line an even number of times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A closed walk crosses each vertical line `x = m + 1/2` an even number of times.

results.title: Interior cells by the even-odd rule

results.title: Finiteness of the interior of a closed walk

results.title: Finite set of interior cells of a closed walk

results.title: Corner count of the interior counts inside cells around a point

results.summary: The corner count of the interior at `(vx, vy)` counts the inside cells among the four cells around that point.

results.title: Ray parity is constant around a non-vertex point

results.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the east direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a left turn made of a south step followed by an east step, the corner weight of the interior is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

results.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the north direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a left turn made of an east step followed by a north step, the corner weight of the interior is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

results.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the south direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a left turn made of a west step followed by a south step, the corner weight of the interior is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

results.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the west direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a left turn made of a north step followed by a west step, the corner weight of the interior is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

results.title: A horizontal direction is not vertical
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A horizontal direction is not vertical.

results.title: A vertical direction is not horizontal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vertical direction is not horizontal.

results.title: Even corner counts have zero corner weight

results.summary: An even corner count has weight `0`.

results.title: Zero corner weight where the walk continues horizontally

results.summary: A vertex where the walk continues horizontally has weight `0`.

results.title: Zero corner weight where the walk continues vertically
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vertex where the walk continues vertically has weight `0`.

results.title: Straight steps of a simple closed walk carry no corner weight

results.title: Horizontal neighbours of different parity are separated by a vertical step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` have different ray parities, a vertical step separates them.

results.title: Vertical neighbours of different parity are separated by a horizontal step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` have different ray parities, a horizontal step separates them.

results.title: Interior of a simple closed walk has no pinch points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The interior of a simple closed walk has no pinch points.

results.title: Pinch count of the ray-parity interior is zero

results.summary: The interior of a simple closed walk has pinch count `0`. See also `StatMech.Onsager.WalkCellLocal.pinchCount_interiorCells_eq_zero`.

results.title: Zero corner weight of the interior off the walk

results.summary: A lattice point off the walk has corner weight `0` for the interior.

results.title: Corner defect of the interior as a sum over walk vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple closed walk, the corner defect of the interior is the sum of the corner weights at the walk vertices.

results.title: Corner weights at the turns of a walk without right turns
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The corner weight of the interior at the vertex after step `i` is `±1` (sign given by the orientation) at a left turn and `0` at a straight step.

results.title: Corner defect of the interior is the number of left turns up to sign
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The corner defect of the interior equals `±cc d`, the sign given by the orientation of the walk.

results.title: Four left turns from a pinch-free interior of Euler characteristic 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A simple closed walk without right turns whose interior is pinch-free with Euler characteristic `1` has four left turns.

results.title: Vertex of a walk as a lattice site

results.title: Vertices of a simple walk are distinct sites

results.summary: The vertices of a simple walk are distinct sites.

results.title: Each lattice step has $\ell^1$-length one

results.summary: Each step of the walk is an edge of its image graph.

results.title: Neighbours in the image graph are walk predecessor and successor

results.title: Horizontally face-adjacent cells have the same ray parity

results.title: Membership in the bounded face

results.title: Face-graph component of an interior cell

results.title: A side between interior and exterior cells is a walk edge
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A side shared by an interior and an exterior cell is an edge of the walk.

results.title: Three walk edges cannot meet at a vertex

results.title: Cell to the left of a walk step

results.title: Cell to the right of a walk step
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the image graph of a simple closed walk, a vertex is adjacent only to its walk neighbours.

results.title: Consecutive left cells on a straight step are face-adjacent

results.title: Every left cell lies in the bounded face
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every left cell of a simple closed walk without right turns lies in the bounded face.

results.title: Cells on either side of a step lie in different faces

results.summary: The two cells on either side of a walk step are in different face components.

results.summary: The left and right cells of a step are adjacent faces sharing that step.
